state.objective: Plan, without implementing, a Can replacement for every test harness under /tests and any external harness logic supplying its coverage. The clarified requirements permit a non-TypeScript testing engine and demand support for any normal Can helper function. Native language/platform infrastructure is allowed, but encoding former test sequences or expected-result judgments inside native adapters would merely relocate the forbidden harness.
state.frontend: Today the checker is implemented in Go and yields Program containing functions, assertions, executable entry regions, native definitions and specialized calls. Its typed IR models closure captures, invocation setup, calls, matches, error and completion branches, and coordinated work. The same checked program feeds TypeScript/Bun generation for both assertion and production entry modes. No runnable interpreter for general Can was identified in the compiler code examined.
state.semantics: An alternative full-language engine inherits contracts for bigint math, Object.is treatment of floats, Bun.deepEquals-based deep/nominal equality, opaque/callable identity and captured environments. It also must implement individual domain/standard failure occurrences, FIFO fixtures, raw exchanges, asynchronous coordination and resource ownership/lifetimes. Assertion actual and expected values both come from executable regions of IR. Evaluating a small declarative test registry is insufficient for this scope.
state.current_execution: Bounded Bun worker isolation, timeout handling and process reaping already exist in the Go assertion supervisor. Its input/output model targets assertion roots and would need a different live-suite protocol. Live subprocess, filesystem and JSON work can be written in ordinary Can main, whereas attached asserts intentionally refuse real platform effects. There is neither a general finally construct nor a guarantee that local timers interrupt non-yielding execution or that killed programs finish cleanup.
state.ownership: Each candidate architecture leaves test discovery/selection, fixture policy, action sequencing, scheduler policy, expected outcomes, comparisons, verdicts and report decisions in Can. Generic native containment may manage child existence, enforce bounds and carry messages; timeout/crash observations go back to Can policy. Internal plans can annotate calls to arbitrary Can bodies, but a limited test language, incomplete evaluator or concealed delegation of test decisions to host code cannot satisfy the user.
state.gaps: Every approach requires new suite communication, supervised temporary-directory ownership, child descriptor/signal control, browser automation and independent native/SQL observation interfaces. Those interfaces may expose primitive actions and raw facts, never an old scenario bundled with an answer. browser::* currently operates within the page DOM rather than remotely driving browsers. Picking another execution target leaves this capability work outstanding.
state.trust: Tests of shipped code generation and runtime still have to send subject fixtures through the production TypeScript/Bun toolchain and run those outputs. An interpreter offers a different execution implementation but retains common parser/checker/IR assumptions, so it cannot provide total independence. Identify a trusted runner compiler or executor by digest apart from the candidate; keep independent expected vectors, failure-seeded cases and distinct full, partial and blocked evidence. Do not equate a coordinator passing on another backend with production qualification.
state.limits: With no external users, historical syntax/ABI compatibility is not required. Disk capacity is 256 GB, laptop workload must stay bounded, and neither benchmarks nor broad builds should run during this design round. Claims of faster startup or reduced CPU/storage are untested. Limit job count, elapsed time, output and storage; attach cleanup on allocation and recover abandoned resources only after ownership/inactivity checks. One run may reuse artifacts, but persistent private bundles and dependency clones are excluded. Prefer the least implementation and semantic upkeep compatible with full-language behavior, coverage and containment.

backend.instructions: Assess the alternatives as a first architecture for retiring host harnesses while allowing arbitrary Can code, retaining Can-authored judgments and production validation, and controlling engineering plus machine cost. Base the choice on the provided implementation evidence, without inventing benchmark results or completed platform features.

criteria.supervised_bun: Keep the existing compiler/runtime for arbitrary Can suite functions and emit their TypeScript/Bun form, placing generic process supervision, hard bounds and cleanup around workers. Let Can specify fixtures, ordering, scheduling policy and verdicts; distinguish the known-good runner from the compiler under test. Supply the missing protocol and native operations without duplicating Can execution semantics.
criteria.full_ir_interpreter: Run all normal test-side Can in a new Go interpreter over typed IR, implementing the complete language plus platform/native behavior. Give the interpreter external isolation and explicit provenance; preserve Can decisions and route tested artifacts through the production TypeScript/Bun backend. Invest in a second maintained runtime so test functions need no TypeScript lowering.
criteria.native_codegen: Introduce a complete native compilation route for Can tests, including a new runtime and platform implementations. It must handle arbitrary helpers, retain scenario/verdict logic in Can and run under bounded supervision with known origin. Test subjects continue their production TypeScript/Bun route; accept an additional backend project to obtain native test executables.
criteria.undetermined: Defer selecting a preferred execution path: an important missing piece of evidence requires targeted research before a starting recommendation is defensible.
